questions.question: What kind of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency brakes must use mechanical force to work reliably.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions need double clutching to shift gears. This technique takes practice to master.

questions.question: Older trailers without spring brakes will have no brakes if the air supply leaks away. What happens?

options.text: The trailer will not have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will not have brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away, the trailer loses all braking power. The wheels will turn freely without any brakes.

questions.question: When coupling air hoses, you should:

options.text: Connect the correct glad hands together.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the correct glad hands together.
questions.explanation: Match the correct pairs of glad hands when coupling. They are sometimes color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: What happens to shaded areas of a road?

options.text: They are blocked from moisture and cannot freeze.
They stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and warm up slowly. They stay icy and slippery after ice has melted on other parts of the road.

questions.question: When stopping in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Veer the trailer right and stop.
Veer the trailer left and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a straight line. You can use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep the vehicle straight but be ready to turn if you need to.

questions.question: You should use the speed of other vehicles to decide when to upshift.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your manual for the rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Know which speeds each gear handles and watch the speedometer to shift as needed.

questions.question: Why must you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs replacing
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a type of retarder?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air
questions.explanation: Retarders slow down a vehicle and reduce the need for braking. The four basic types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Will stop turn signals from working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a potentially serious problem.
questions.explanation: The suspension system keeps the axles in place. Damaged suspension parts like leaking shock absorbers are potentially dangerous and should be fixed.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which of the following should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your high beam lights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and turn on your flashers and low beam headlights. Do not use high beam lights.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air filter
questions.explanation: An air brake system includes an air compressor, storage tanks, gauges, warning devices, and spring brakes. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: What is true about doubles and triples?

options.text: They turn easily because of their centers of gravity.
They are harder to turn than smaller commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to turn than smaller commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because of their size, doubles and triples are difficult to turn. They need extra care to prevent rollovers when turning.

questions.question: Is it good to keep space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: Yes, it gives you time to react to unexpected hazards.
Only if you are traveling with a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it gives you time to react to unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires keeping space around your vehicle on all sides. This space gives you time to react if a problem occurs.

questions.question: How can a driver test the coupling?

options.text: By placing their fingers inside the coupling mechanism.
By pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.
By placing glue over the fifth wheel.
By releasing the orange lever in the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: By pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.
questions.explanation: Before starting a trip, a driver should inspect the coupling. Test the coupling on doubles and triples by pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.

questions.question: What should a driver do to prevent a rollover?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo low.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when vehicles turn too quickly. Keep the vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: What equipment must a commercial motor vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if transporting hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes a fire extinguisher, reflective triangles or flares, and spare fuses.

questions.question: What happens when brakes are out of adjustment?

options.text: Some brakes overwork and can break down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes overwork and can break down.
questions.explanation: Out of adjustment brakes fail before properly adjusted ones. Check brake adjustment frequently to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: What is true about doubles combinations?

options.text: They are less likely to jackknife than single trailers.
They are less likely to roll over than single trailers.
They require more reaction time than single trailers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require more reaction time than single trailers.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples are more likely to jackknife and roll over than single trailers. Drivers should look far ahead and react to hazards early by slowing down or changing lanes gradually.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They allow rain water to enter air tanks.
They remove water and oil from air tanks.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If these build up, they can damage the air brake system.
